 AFCON 2027 (Q): Namibia coach Collin Benjamin set to miss clash against Cameroon
 📅 November 16, 2026 
  • 
 👤 Kabuma Node 
  • 
 📁 AFCON 
  • 
 🕑 2 min read 
 Namibia national team Brave Warriors head coach Collin Benjamin will be unavailable for Monday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier against Cameroon at 15h00 due to personal reasons.
 Assistant coach John Sikerete will take charge of the national team from the touchline for the fixture. Benjamin’s absence is limited to Monday’s match, with the coach expected to return to the technical team thereafter. Cameroon moved to the top of Group G with seven points from three matches after a convincing 2-0 home victory over Namibia.
 The Indomitable Lions took control early in Douala, with Saidou Alioum opening the scoring in the 16th minute when his effort took a wicked deflection on its way into the net.
 Bil Nsongo doubled their advantage in the 29th minute with a more emphatic finish, leaving Namibia with a mountain to climb. The visitors struggled to create clear scoring opportunities against a well-organised Cameroon defence, and the hosts remained in control as they completed a comfortable victory.
 Cameroon have now opened a four-point advantage over second-placed Comoros, although the island nation have played one match fewer.
